The healthcare Q&A matches suggest that the concept of "pneumologist's skepticism" in relation to chemotherapy and its impact on survival in patients with advanced non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC) is a topic of discussion among experts.

In normal clinical practice, chemotherapy does significantly prolong survival in patients with poor performance status, including those without weight loss. However, the question of whether this attitude towards chemotherapy is justified remains. 

The matches indicate that while many pneumologists are skeptical about using chemotherapy for advanced NSCLC due to concerns about its effectiveness and potential side effects, the actual data suggest that this skepticism may be misplaced. The majority of patients with tumors less than 3 cm in size, those with adenocarcinoma histologic type, and those without negative bronchial resection margins tend to have better outcomes when treated with chemotherapy.

It is worth noting that a more effective multimodal treatment approach is needed to increase survival rates in NSCLC. Additionally, the collection of patients' self-reported health-related quality of life data can provide independent prognostic information for survival.

In terms of whether tumor expression of VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor) is associated with venous invasion and survival in pT3 renal cell carcinoma, there is no clear correlation between these factors. 

Regarding the use of neoadjuvant chemotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, it appears that this approach can improve both survival and disease control.

Finally, regarding whether quality of life in lung cancer patients depends on socioeconomic status, the results suggest that while lower socioeconomic status has been associated with lower health-related quality of life, there is no clear trend at follow-up assessment. This implies that patients from different socioeconomic backgrounds may respond similarly to treatment, suggesting that quality of life is influenced by individual factors rather than their social context.

Overall, the healthcare Q&A matches indicate that the concept of "pneumologist's skepticism" regarding chemotherapy and its impact on survival in advanced NSCLC needs further clarification. While some pneumologists may have concerns about chemotherapy, the actual data suggest that this approach can be effective for certain patient groups. The importance of a more comprehensive treatment approach, including multimodal therapy, to improve outcomes cannot be overstated.

It is essential to consider patients' quality of life as well, rather than solely focusing on survival rates, in order to provide better care and support for lung cancer patients.
